drivingQuestion: In which places, times, animals and limbs does the prohibition of the sciatic nerve apply, and are butchers deemed credible about its removal?
outcomeNote: Mishna text only (the unit opens the chapter Gid HaNasheh after the הדרן closing the previous chapter); two tannaitic disputes are stated and left unresolved, with no gemara discussion in this unit.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת, בַּחוּלִּין וּבַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין, וְנוֹהֵג בִּבְהֵמָה וּבְחַיָּה, בְּיָרֵךְ שֶׁל יָמִין וּבְיָרֵךְ שֶׁל שְׂמֹאל, וְאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בָּעוֹף – מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ כַּף.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» The prohibition of eating «the sciatic nerve applies» both «in Eretz» Yisrael «and outside of Eretz» Yisrael, «in the presence of,» i.e., the time of, «the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple,» and «with regard to non-sacred» animals «and with regard to sacrificial» animals. «And it applies to domesticated animals and to undomesticated animals, to» the «thigh of the right» leg «and to» the «thigh of the left» leg. «But it does not apply to a bird, due to» the fact «that» the verse makes reference to the sciatic nerve as being “upon the spoon of the thigh” (Genesis 32:33), and a bird «has no spoon» of the thigh.

segments.he: וְנוֹהֵג בַּשְּׁלִיל. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בַּשְּׁלִיל, וְחֶלְבּוֹ מוּתָּר.
segments.en: And the prohibition «applies to» a late-term animal «fetus [shalil]» in the womb. «Rabbi Yehuda says: It does not apply to a fetus; and» similarly, «its fat is permitted.»

segments.he: וְאֵין הַטַּבָּחִין נֶאֱמָנִין עַל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמָנִין עָלָיו וְעַל הַחֵלֶב.
segments.en: «And butchers are not deemed credible» to say that «the sciatic nerve» was removed; this is «the statement of Rabbi Meir. And the Rabbis say: They are deemed credible about» the sciatic nerve «and about the» forbidden «fat.»

moves.cueHe: גיד הנשה נוהג בארץ ובחוצה לארץ
moves.summary: the mishna states the full scope of the sciatic-nerve prohibition — everywhere, at all times, non-sacred and sacrificial, both kinds of animal, both thighs — and excludes birds, which have no spoon of the thigh
the enumeration of scope continues: the prohibition applies also to a fetus in the womb
moves.about: whether the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies to a late-term fetus (שליל) in the womb — the first tanna says it does, Rabbi Yehuda says it does not (and adds that the fetus's fat is permitted)

moves.summary: Rabbi Yehuda rules against the first tanna: the prohibition does not apply to a fetus, and its fat is permitted

moves.cueHe: ואין הטבחין נאמנין על גיד הנשה
moves.summary: a new topic in the mishna: Rabbi Meir rules that butchers are not credible about removal of the sciatic nerve
moves.about: whether butchers are deemed credible to say that they removed the sciatic nerve (and the forbidden fat) from meat they sell

moves.summary: the Sages rule against Rabbi Meir: butchers are credible both about the sciatic nerve and about the forbidden fat

edges.cueHe: רבי יהודה אומר: אינו נוהג בשליל
edges.about: whether the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies to a late-term fetus (שליל) in the womb — the first tanna says it does, Rabbi Yehuda says it does not (and adds that the fetus's fat is permitted)

edges.cueHe: וחכמים אומרים: נאמנין עליו ועל החלב
edges.about: whether butchers are deemed credible to say that they removed the sciatic nerve (and the forbidden fat) from meat they sell
